content.overview: Vicarious liability makes one person answerable for the tort of another because of their relationship—classically an employer for a servant's tort committed in the course of employment—without the employer necessarily being personally at fault.
content.study: First establish the primary tort (often negligence). Then ask: is the wrongdoer a servant or an independent contractor, and was the act in the course of employment (including wrongful modes of authorised acts and, in some lines, close connection with assigned duties)? Distinguish from direct negligence of the employer (hiring, systems, supervision). Pair with negligence as the usual underlying wrong.
